$comment: Game time, PRD section 2. A day lasts about as long as a brig's real day's run (~115 tiles at ~4.5 tiles/s): 771 ticks at 30 per second is about 26 s at 1x, 13 s at the default 2x cruise. The sailing pace is 0.7 of the original, so the day is 1/0.7 as long and voyages, seasons and every rate measured in days are unchanged. The time of day is a clock of its own, slower than the date: a game day passes in under half a minute, too fast for sunrise and sunset to be seen, so the light keeps a long day (daylight.phases: game seconds at 1x, and the hours each shows: a short golden dawn, a long bright day, a golden dusk and a short moonlit night), about twenty minutes at 1x, faster when time is sped up, still while the game is paused. The sky, the coastal breezes, how far a ship is seen, the music and the harbour paintings all keep this one clock. A new game opens daylight.startSeconds into it, mid-morning.
